title: Bebop band with Clarence Ford and abandoning the old musicians
summary: Formed the Bebop Jockeys, dropped older players, and almost lost his house; returned to Dixieland.

bands.name: Wallace Davenport and His Bebop Jockeys

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: was playing. But all three of us had teachers. Did you have a band with Clarence Ford?

Oh yeah, yeah. That's when I came out of the service. We had also created by Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker. I called all the old musicians up whom I played with and told them I didn't want to play with them no more. That's because the music you're playing is old, that's out of style. I'm playing bebop now. So Clarence Ford, we graduated from high school together. From Booker T. Washington? Yeah, same class. And Wilbur Hogan too. Did you have him? Yeah. Wilbur Hogan? Yeah. We graduated together. And he, what did I say?
You were talking about Clarence Ford and you know how?

Oh yeah, yeah. So we was playing bebop. So we'd buy Dizzy Gillespie records and Charlie Parker records and we'd rehearse them. And we'd call, the name of the band was Wallace Devin Bode and his bebop jockeys. And we, I called all those old musicians up and told them I didn't talk with them anymore. So. How did that go over? Bad. Bad. Because I wasn't making any money. I bought a house. And I was fixing to lose my house. Didn't have any food to eat. Didn't have any food to eat. My wife, she was Jean, she was just as crazy as I was. Wallace, I don't blame you. She'd say, if I were you I wouldn't play with them old men. See at that time those guys were like in their thirties and I was in my twenties. But you'd heard this new music. Yeah. I thought that. And what did you think? I heard this new music and I found out you had to really practice to play that music and study. Which I was accustomed to doing, you know, practicing and studying. But these older musicians they were just going to the job and playing. Most of them couldn't read music play. So, when I decided, I said no, I'm not going to lose my house. So I went out on the river front. One of those guys picking those big sacks. Sure. And when I went out there and when I got to the door I saw a big guy, looked like he was a wrestler, looked like Hulk Hogan or somebody, with his big sack on it and he was badly making it. I stepped up and looked at him. I said no, I'm going back and started playing Dixieland again. I came back home and told all the old guys, look man I'm ready to play with you guys again. Because I didn't want to lose my house. And I was too small. At that time I was weighing about a hundred and forty-two pounds. And I couldn't pick up those big sacks like that. So you said you owned your house by this time.
